head: Giants made steel from ore.
Nucor melted scrap.
slides.sub: How small mills beat America's steel titans.

image.label: Sparks pouring from an electric furnace in a small steel mill
image.brief: 작은 제강공장 안, 전기로에서 쏟아지는 주황빛 불꽃. 1970년대 미국 남부 공장 분위기. 작업자는 실루엣으로만. 로고 없음.

head: A small company
that needed steel.
body: In the 1960s, Nucor was a struggling firm whose best business, Vulcraft, made steel joists for buildings. Ken Iverson, who ran the company, was tired of buying steel at the big mills' prices.
In 1969, Nucor opened its own mill in Darlington, South Carolina.

image.label: Steel joists stacked at a rural 1960s plant
image.brief: 1960년대 미국 남부 시골 공장 마당에 쌓인 철골 장선. 흙길, 낮은 창고 건물, 따뜻한 오후 빛.

head: No blast furnace.
Just scrap and power.
body: The big integrated steelmakers turned iron ore and coal into steel in giant blast furnaces that cost fortunes to build.
Nucor's minimill used an electric arc furnace to melt scrap, like old cars and machinery. It was smaller and far cheaper to build, but at first it could only make simpler products like bars.

image.label: A scrap yard of crushed cars next to a compact mill
image.brief: 찌그러진 폐차와 고철 더미 옆의 아담한 제강공장. 멀리 거대한 고로 굴뚝이 대비되는 구도.

slides.label: layers of management between a mill worker and the CEO
body: Nucor kept headquarters tiny and paid crews weekly bonuses tied to the good steel they shipped. Reportedly, bonuses could match or beat base pay. Executives got no company jets or private dining rooms.

image.label: A plain small office with a few desks
image.brief: 책상 몇 개뿐인 소박한 본사 사무실. 화려한 장식 없음. 1980년대 톤.

head: The giants let go.
Nucor moved up.
body: Low-end products earned thin margins, so the integrated mills were happy to give them up and focus on higher-value steel.
Each time they stepped back, minimills moved into the next product: bars, then angles, then structural beams. The giants' last stronghold was sheet steel for cars and appliances.

image.label: A staircase of steel products rising from bars to beams
image.brief: 철근, 앵글, H빔이 계단처럼 점점 높아지는 구성. 맨 위는 빈 자리로 남겨둠.

head: Sheet steel needs giant mills.
What do you do?
body: It's the late 1980s. Sheet steel is the most valuable market, and no minimill can make it. A new German thin-slab casting method promises a way in, but it is unproven at scale.

options.text: Stay in bars and beams, where you already win
options.feedback: Safe and profitable, but it leaves the biggest market to the giants for good. Keep swiping.

options.text: Buy an old integrated mill to get into sheet
options.feedback: Fast entry, but you inherit the high costs you've spent years beating. Keep swiping.

options.text: Bet a new mill on the untested thin-slab caster
options.feedback: A huge capital bet on technology no one had made work commercially. Keep swiping.

image.label: Coils of sheet steel behind a locked gate
image.brief: 잠긴 철문 너머로 보이는 강판 코일 더미. 차가운 청회색 조명.

slides.label: minimill to make sheet steel from thin slabs, in Crawfordsville, Indiana, 1989
body: Nucor chose the bet. After a difficult start-up, the plant worked. Minimills could now compete in the market the giants had kept for themselves.

image.label: A thin glowing slab of steel moving through rollers
image.brief: 롤러 위를 지나가는 얇고 붉게 달아오른 강판. 인디애나 평야 위 공장 외관이 배경에 살짝.

head: The titans retreated
until there was no room.
body: Nucor built more sheet mills through the 1990s and became one of the largest steelmakers in America.
Meanwhile, integrated giants carried heavy costs they couldn't shed. Around 2000 and 2001, LTV Steel and Bethlehem Steel filed for bankruptcy.

image.label: A rusting blast furnace beside a modern compact mill
image.brief: 녹슨 거대 고로와 그 옆에 새로 지은 깔끔한 소형 제강공장. 해 질 녘.

head: Start where giants won't fight.
Climb from there.
body: Nucor entered the low end with a cheaper way to make steel. Each retreat by the incumbents looked sensible, because it raised their margins. Together, those retreats gave the market away.
Lean costs and pay tied to output kept Nucor cheaper at every step.

image.label: A small arrow climbing past a large stalled one
image.brief: 작은 화살표가 멈춰 선 큰 화살표를 지나 위로 올라가는 그래픽. 강철 질감.

head: The market you give up
can be a rival's ladder.
body: Dropping low-margin customers feels smart each time. Watch who picks them up, and what they learn on the way.
**Try it today:** list the customers you've stopped serving. Who serves them now, and how much cheaper are they?

image.label: A single steel beam against an evening sky
image.brief: 저녁 하늘을 배경으로 한 철골 빔 하나. 단순하고 힘 있는 구도.

factChecks.note: Nucor(옛 Nuclear Corporation of America)의 첫 제강공장이 1969년 사우스캐롤라이나 다링턴에서 가동됐고, 자회사 Vulcraft의 철골 장선(joist)용 철강을 자체 조달하려는 목적이었다는 점은 Nucor 공식 연혁으로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1969년 사우스캐롤라이나 다링턴 첫 제강공장 확인.
Ken Iverson이 1965년 무렵 회사 경영을 맡았다는 시점은 Nucor 연혁과 Iverson의 책 'Plain Talk'(1998)로 확인하세요. 카드에는 연도를 넣지 않고 '1960s'로만 적었습니다.

현장 직원과 CEO 사이 관리 계층이 4단계(감독자-부서장-공장장-사장)였다는 내용은 'Plain Talk' 등 Iverson의 설명 기준입니다. 보너스가 기본급에 맞먹거나 넘을 수 있었다는 점은 'reportedly'로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] CEO와 현장 사이 관리 계층 4단계 확인(IndustryWeek, 5단계로 적은 자료도 있음).
인디애나주 크로퍼즈빌 공장(1989)이 독일 SMS의 박슬래브 연속주조 기술로 미니밀 최초로 평판(시트) 강재를 생산했다는 점은 Nucor 연혁과 Ghemawat의 HBS 사례 연구로 확인하세요. 투자액은 자료마다 달라 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1989년 크로퍼즈빌, 박슬래브 방식 세계 최초 미니밀 평판 생산 확인.
대형 일관제철소들이 마진이 낮은 봉강 등 하위 제품에서 물러나며 상위 시장으로 이동했다는 서술은 Christensen의 'The Innovator's Dilemma'(1997) 분석 기준입니다.
LTV Steel(2000), Bethlehem Steel(2001) 파산 신청은 당시 주요 언론 보도로 확인하세요. 2000년 무렵 Nucor의 미국 내 순위는 자료에 따라 달라 'one of the largest'로만 적었습니다.

sources.text: Iverson, K. (1998). Plain Talk: Lessons from a Business Maverick. Wiley.
Christensen, C. (1997). The Innovator's Dilemma. Harvard Business School Press.
Ghemawat, P. Nucor at a Crossroads. Harvard Business School case study.
Nucor: The evolution of America's leading steelmaker
